title: Stateful runtime upgrade and DB migration playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for upgrading stateful inference runtimes in private deployments (VPC and on-prem) where we must also migrate persistent state/databases and ensure API compatibility with older clients. Focus is on minimal downtime, safe rollback, and Terraform state hygiene.

Audience:
SRE/Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers running customer on-prem upgrades, Release Engineers coordinating rollouts with Customers.

High-level goals:
- Upgrade runtime binary & model-serving kernels with minimal disruption to live traffic.
- Apply required DB schema changes with reversible migrations.
- Keep control plane and client API compatibility checks in the loop.
- Maintain clear Terraform state migration steps for module refactors.
- Provide explicit rollback steps and signal checks.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customer runs private-control-plane version X.Y or earlier; we are upgrading to X.(Y+1).
- Databases: Postgres for metadata, RocksDB/LMDB for local KV cache on nodes (or S3 for cluster-backed caches).
- Nodes are Kubernetes clusters (kubeadm / customer-managed), but air-gapped customers may run systemd-based runtime clusters.
- Access: SRE has bastion access and KMS credentials where necessary.

Pre-upgrade checklist (must be done 48–72 hours before cutover):
- Confirm backup: full pg_dump of metadata DB and filesystem copy of KV stores. Command examples:
  - pg_dump -Fc -f /backups/metadata-YYYYMMDD.dump redwood_metadata
  - rsync -av --progress /var/lib/redwood/kv /backups/kv-YYYYMMDD
- Validate restore procedure in staging with a copy of the prod DB (at least once in last 30 days).
- Collect live metrics and traces (last 72h) for baseline: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token throughput.
- Notify customer and stakeholders; schedule maintenance window (2–6 hours depending on DB size).
- Ensure Terraform state is healthy and remote backend accessible. Run: terraform plan and terraform state list.
- Flag incompatible plugins/modules in Terraform (terraform providers lockfile).
- Create a canary cluster/namespace that mirrors production config for a sanity run.

Runtime upgrade steps (day of cutover):
1) Prepare control plane and canary
   - Deploy new control-plane version to canary namespace. Run smoke tests against canary endpoints.
   - Validate API responses using integration test suite (api-compat-checker).
2) Quiesce non-critical consumers
   - Temporarily route lower-tier traffic to fallback model or hosted API. Update routing policies in the control plane.
3) Drain one node/pool and upgrade runtime binary
   - kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - Stop local runtime: systemctl stop redwood-runtime || kubectl apply -f runtime-deploy-vX.Y+1.yaml
   - Apply schema migrations if this node is primary for DB writes (see DB step ordering).
   - Start runtime and run healthcheck: /opt/redwood/bin/healthcheck --full
   - Rejoin node to pool: kubectl uncordon <node>
   - Observe metrics for 10–30 minutes. If errors spike, follow node rollback steps below.
4) Canary rollout across node pool
   - Repeat for 2–3 canary nodes across AZs. Expand to 10% of nodes, then 30%, then 100% with monitoring gates.

DB migration strategy (safe & reversible):
- Use online, backward-compatible migrations when possible: add columns with NULL/default, create new tables, deploy code that writes both old and new schema, then migrate reads.
- Migration phases:
  A) Schema additive changes (safe): deploy code compatible with both schemas, run migration to add columns/indexes.
  B) Data backfill (bulk): schedule off-peak, use chunked updates with LIMIT/OFFSET or keyrange to avoid long locks.
  C) Switch read path: flip feature-flag to start reading from new columns/tables.
  D) Cleanup: after 7+ days of stable traffic and verification, remove legacy columns.

Example Postgres migration commands (chuck-wise updates):
- Add column: ALTER TABLE job_runs ADD COLUMN model_version TEXT;
- Backfill in chunks:
  - psql -c "BEGIN; UPDATE job_runs SET model_version = 'v2' WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM job_runs WHERE model_version IS NULL LIMIT 10000 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); COMMIT;"
- Monitor long-running queries via pg_stat_activity; set statement_timeout for safety.

Terraform module notes and state migration (common pitfalls):
- When renaming a module or refactoring resources, use terraform state mv to avoid recreation. Example: terraform state mv module.old_pool.kubernetes_deployment.redwood module.new_pool.kubernetes_deployment.redwood
- For provider upgrades, run terraform init -upgrade in a sandbox with a copy of state first.
- If remote backend is S3/GCS, take a snapshot of state file before migration.
- Document changed resource addresses in the PR and in this playbook for easy audit.
- If customers run local terraform with different provider versions, include provider constraints and a migration guide in the PR.

API compatibility checklist (control plane + client):
- Run api-compat-checker between old and new control plane versions with recorded request sets.
- Validate function/tool calling signatures and structured output fields.
- If breaking change is unavoidable, provide compatibility shim: API v1 -> v2 translation layer inside control plane.
- Update SDK docs and patch notes; include migration examples for customers.

Smoke tests and verification (post-upgrade):
- Generate synthetic traffic using the production prompt set and compare p50/p95 latency and error rates to baseline.
- Run deterministic evals for output quality regression.
- Check KV cache hit rates and token throughput.
- Validate model alias routing and pinned model versions.
- Verify audit logs and KMS-integrated key usage for new runtime.

Rollback plan (node-level and global):
Node-level rollback (if a single node behaves badly):
- cordon & drain node; kubectl apply previous deployment manifest or systemctl start redwood-runtime@<previous-version>
- If DB migration applied on that node only for local state, restore local KV from backup.

Global rollback (if widespread regression):
- Immediately pause rollout and route traffic to dedicated fallback:
  - Update routing policy: route->fallback-model or hosted API
  - Re-run terraform to re-deploy previous control plane version: terraform apply -var 'control_plane_version=X.Y' -target=module.control_plane
- Revert schema changes only if they are destructive: restore metadata DB from pg_dump snapshot to a point-in-time. NOTE: full DB restore is disruptive and should be last resort.
- Communicate to stakeholders and customers with expected RTO/RPO.

Postmortem signals and data collection (if rollback occurs):
- Collect: runtime logs (journalctl or pod logs), DB slow query logs, control plane traces, metric snapshots, and failed request examples.
- Triage owners: runtime lead, DB lead, control plane lead.

Air-gapped / on-prem specific notes:
- Ensure all container images and packages are mirrored in customer registry ahead of time.
- Provide an offline migration bundle: binaries, manifests, migration SQL, and a small helper script.
- Test the bundle in customer's staging environment at least once.
- If KMS/HSM is customer-managed, coordinate key rotation and ensure new runtime has access to the correct key alias.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide safe max chunk size for backfills for very large metadata DBs (>1TB).
- Determine a standardized wait window between schema change and removal of legacy fields (proposal: 7–14 days).
- Add a small utility to automatically snapshot RocksDB directories and validate integrity.
- Formalize api-compat-checker results into a standardized release gate metric.

Quick rollback command recipes (for runbook):
- Terraform state snapshot: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-terraform-prod/state.tfstate /backups/state-YYYYMMDD.tfstate
- Move resource in state: terraform state mv old.address new.address
- Restore Postgres from dump: pg_restore -d redwood_metadata -C /backups/metadata-YYYYMMDD.dump
- Drain a node: kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m

Notes from past upgrades (lessons learned):
- Always verify remote backend credentials up-front; missing access cost us 2 hours in a past upgrade.
- Small canaries across AZs surface cross-AZ config bugs fast.
- Background backfills caused CPU saturation on DB primary once — set CPU cgroup limits for migration jobs.

Appendix: useful links and commands
- GH PR with module refactor: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987
- Jira deployment ticket template: JIRA-DEPLOY-TEMPLATE
- api-compat-checker: ./tools/api-compat-checker --baseline vX.Y --target vX.Y+1 --requests requests.json

End of draft. This document is a working playbook — expect edits and additions.
